newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland Bank sees 4 pct 1997 growth, low inflation.
newsitem.headline: Finland Bank sees 4 pct 1997 growth, low inflation.

text.p: Bank of Finland governor Sirkka Hamalainen said on Friday Finnish gross domestic product growth could accelerate to four percent this year from nearly three percent in 1996, and that inflation would remain slow.
In a statement with the central bank's 1996 accounts, Hamalainen also said Finland was likely to meet all convergence criteria for the third stage of Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
"The growth of total output could reach four percent in 1997," Hamalainen said. "Total output is estimated to have grown by nearly three percent," she said referring to 1996.
"It appears that the rise (in 1997) in the price level will stay near the targeted level," Hamalainen said.
"The consumer price index rose by about one percent in 1996, and the indicator of underlying inflation, which serves as a basis for monetary policy, was even more subdued," she added.
The Bank of Finland's inflation target is for an annual rise in underlying inflation of no more than about two percent on average.
Hamalainen said the decline in unemployment was likely to continue, but still "at a very sluggish pace."
"It appears that Finland will be able to meet all the economic convergence criteria for EMU," she said.

Pointing at Finland's decision in October 1996 to link the markka to the European Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM), Hamalainen said the purpose had been "to ensure its eligibility" to be among the first countries to move into stage three of EMU.
